adapter.name: stanag4609
adapter.why_the_two_names_differ: The adapter takes the STANAG's number because STANAG 4609 is, in MISP-2019.1 SS C.1.2's own words, 'a covering document rather than a standalone document, which points directly to a version of the U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Profile (MISP)' - so there is no NATO document whose CONTENT could name the adapter, while the STANAG number is what an ICD, a NISP row and a national ratification record all call the feed. The fixture directory takes the content's name because a directory holds PAYLOADS and a payload is not a standard, which is the same split that puts adapter stanag4676's fixtures in fixtures/nits. The adapter-shaped content is the KLV metadata stream, so the directory is klv and the payload extension will be .klv.

rejected_directory_names.misp: Names the governing profile, which is a DOCUMENT - the pinned PDF would sit at fixtures/misp/spec/misb-misp-2019-1.pdf, a directory named after a file inside it. It also names the wrong layer: the MISP governs the imagery, the audio, the containers and the transport as well, and this adapter reads one of the five.
rejected_directory_names.misb: Names the publisher. fixtures/eurocontrol would have been wrong for CAT048 for the same reason.
rejected_directory_names.fmv: Rejected by the pinned text itself, MISP SS 2.1.1: 'FMV has no formal definition and conveys different meanings to different communities; therefore, the term FMV should not be used in any contractual language.' A fixture directory name is closer to contractual language than to prose.
rejected_directory_names.stanag4609: Would reproduce the bug commit 80b38d1 had to fix - three NITS PDFs sitting in a directory named for the adapter because a copy command took the adapter's name where the fixture directory's name was wanted.

the_normative_act.aim: The aim of this NATO standardization agreement (STANAG) is to respond to the following interoperability requirements.
the_normative_act.interoperability_requirement: To provide common methods for the generation, dissemination, exploitation and archive of Motion Imagery (MI) among National and NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) systems.
the_normative_act.agreement: Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.
the_normative_act.standard: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)
the_normative_act.other_related_documents: U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1): Motion Imagery Handbook
the_normative_act.implementation_of_the_agreement: MISP-2019.1 defines the technical requirements for motion imagery formats, compression, metadata and transmission protocols for ISR systems and systems that manage and/or exploit motion imagery data.
the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical: Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own. Every technical requirement this adapter could implement is in the profile it promulgates, which is why there are two pins and not one.

delegated_specifications_held.what_this_is: The two delegated field dictionaries this round obtained. Both were named by the delegation table below long before either was held; both are now in the working tree, untracked, and pinned here. A pinned document carries THREE facts and this section exists because the pin rows above carried only two: the registry PAGE that is the citable source, the SHA-256 that identifies the COPY that was read, and the EDITION DATE the document states on its own cover.

provenance_ruling.page_as_source: The source of record for a MISB standard is its NSG Registry document page - https://nsgreg.nga.mil/doc/view?i=<n> - and not the URL the bytes arrived over. The page is stable, dereferenceable and states the registry's own view of the document's identity: its version, its registration status and what it supersedes.
provenance_ruling.hash_as_copy: The SHA-256 identifies the COPY THAT WAS READ, which is a different claim from the edition number. This is house style in every pin record here and this round is the first to prove why it is not pedantry: ST 0601.19's cover says 02 March 2023 and the copy on disk carries two amendment rows dated after that, under the same edition number and with no minor-version letter on the cover. The edition number cannot distinguish those two documents. The hash can.
provenance_ruling.why_download_urls_are_not_recorded: The registry serves documents over EPHEMERAL PRESIGNED LINKS. Such a URL expires, so recording one would put a dead string in the source field of a record whose whole purpose is to be checkable years later. The doc/view page is what a reader is sent to; the presigned link is a transport detail of one retrieval.
provenance_ruling.what_the_edition_date_field_means: The date the DOCUMENT states for itself, read off its own cover or front matter, and authoritative for this field where the document states one. Where the registry page states a date too, both are recorded and required to agree - see st_0102_12 below, where three independent statements of 22 June 2017 agree.
provenance_ruling.the_registry_pages_were_not_machine_veri: HONEST LIMIT ON THE SOURCE FIELD. Both doc/view URLs are recorded as the citable source and neither was retrieved by this round: nsgreg.nga.mil answers an automated GET with a CAPTCHA interstitial, so the page's stated version, registration status and supersession line could not be read mechanically. They are recorded as reported. Every fact this round ASSERTS about either document - hash, byte count, page count, edition date, title-page identity - was taken from the bytes on disk instead, which is the stronger source for those five and the reason the ruling below does not rest on the registry at all. The parks' reopen route is unaffected: a CAPTCHA is a bot gate, not an account gate, and a person with a browser is not blocked.

reconciliation_ruling.what_this_is: THE RULING THAT GATES THE TAG TABLES, and it had to exist before any tag table was transcribed, because it is what decides which tag table is authoritative. The question: MISP-2019.1 is the profile STANAG 4609 Edition 5 promulgates, and it pins specific revisions of the documents it delegates to. Do the copies this round obtained match the revisions the profile pins? One ruling per document, and the answers differ.
reconciliation_ruling.method: MISP-2019.1's normative reference list is its Appendix B, PDF pages 63-66. It was read in full and its entries numbered by position, because the profile cites references by bracketed number and the extraction drops the brackets. The numbering was validated rather than assumed: parsed positionally it yields 103 entries, which is the count this record already stated from an earlier reading, and it places all sixteen reference numbers this record asserts elsewhere - [1], [13], [14], [48], [53], [54], [55], [56], [57], [59], [65], [70], [72], [73], [75], [76] - on the documents this record already attributes to them. One Appendix B entry omits its terminal full stop (the ITU-T H.265 (V5) entry, which runs into the ISO/IEC 14496-10 entry after it); that is the document's, it shifted the naive count by one, and it is recorded because it is the only reason the first parse disagreed.

ruling_st_0102.ruling: MATCH. The question is closed for this document.
ruling_st_0102.grounds: MISP-2019.1 Appendix B reference [55] pins 0102.12; the copy obtained is 0102.12, its cover states 22 June 2017 and its revision history's single row states the same date. The profile pins this document and this is the document it pins.
ruling_st_0102.what_that_closes: The first half of park 2's exit condition: the EXACT version is obtained and pinned by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read.
ruling_st_0102.what_it_does_not_close: The second half: 'then write the row set that document supports'. That is Act 3, and Act 3 did not run. Park 2 therefore stays in the park table at twelve, and the mapping rows that cite it stay `not yet`. The park is not retired by this commit and the reason is not bookkeeping: the row set is the deliverable and it does not exist yet.
ruling_st_0102.and_it_cannot_be_written_alone_anyway: Even with 0102.12 in hand, a security local set cannot be READ. Its octets are KLV, and KLV encoding is SMPTE ST 336:2017 (park 8, the paywalled one) and KLV formatting in motion imagery is ST 0107.3 (park 4). This record's own smallest_useful_phase_2 states it: 'Parks 4, 5 and 8 are enough to READ a stream at all.' None of those three is held. So the ST 0102 match is real progress on identity and not yet progress on capability.

ruling_st_0601.gap: Five major revisions and roughly four years and four months.
ruling_st_0601.ruling: MISMATCH, and option (b): THE CITED EDITION IS REQUIRED. The round stops here for this document. No tag table is transcribed from 0601.19.
grounds: THE REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY RULED THIS, and consistency is not optional. This record's parks.shared_exit_condition, written in an earlier round and covering parks 1-7 and 9-12, reads: 'obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not "the current one" - the profile pins a revision and a later revision is a different document)'. ST 0601 is park 1. Reading 0601.19 against the profile would overturn a standing ruling in passing, which is the failure mode this record's correction_2026_08_25 field exists to record an instance of.

FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's park 1 row already states the hazard in its own words: 'Version .14 specifically: ST 0601 has revisions on both sides of it, and a tag added in a later revision decoded against an earlier one is a plausible number in the wrong field.' That is not a new argument produced to justify a stop; it is the argument the park was opened with.

OPTION (a) IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM THE COPY IN HAND, which is the decisive practical ground. Option (a) requires recording 'whether any [tags] were added or changed meaning after the cited edition'. ST 0601.19's Table 1 has columns Tag, Name, Units, Format, Len, SDCC, MUL and Description - there is NO column stating which revision introduced an item - and its revision history table carries rows for .19 and its two later amendments and NO rows for .15, .16, .17 or .18. So for any given tag, 'did this exist in .14' cannot be answered from 0601.19 alone. Ruling (a) would mean asserting a delta this round cannot compute.

AND THE HAZARD IS DEMONSTRATED, not hypothetical. 0601.19's revision history records 'Resolved item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)' on 06/11/2025 - a change to what a tag MEANS, on the mean-sea-level-versus-height-above-ellipsoid axis, which is exactly the class of change that yields a plausible number in the wrong field. It also records 'Added Item 143 - Metadata Substream ID (MSID)' for .19 itself. One documented semantic change and one documented addition, inside the only revision window the document describes.
ruling_st_0601.what_the_document_does_let_us_bound: Recorded because it is real and because it is what a later round would start from, NOT as a basis for proceeding. ST 0601 stamps each requirement with the version that introduced it, so the post-.14 REQUIREMENT delta is enumerable from 0601.19 alone: twelve requirements, being ST 0601.15-36, ST 0601.17-37 through ST 0601.17-40, and ST 0601.19-41 through ST 0601.19-47. No requirement names .16 or .18. Appendix A additionally lists retired requirements with the version each came from, including five at ST 0601.14. This bounds the REQUIREMENT delta; it does not bound the ITEM delta, and the item delta is the one a tag table would need.

ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.question: What does the wrapper itself cite for ST 0601 and ST 0102, and does it agree with MISP-2019.1?
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.grounds: STANAG 4609 Edition 5 is five pages and its normative content is read in full. Its AGREEMENT clause reads 'Participating nations agree to implement the following standard' and its STANDARD clause names exactly one document: 'U.S. Motion Imagery Standards Board (MISB) Motion Imagery Standards Profile-2019.1 (MISP-2019.1)'. Its OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS clause names one more, the MISP-2019.1 Motion Imagery Handbook. The strings '0601' and '0102' do not occur in the document at all. It has no reference list of its own.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.ruling: NO CONFLICT TO RECONCILE, and this is a finding rather than an absence of one. The wrapper cites no edition of either document, so it cannot agree or disagree with MISP-2019.1 about one. It delegates the entire question, which makes MISP-2019.1 the SOLE authority for what edition of ST 0601 and ST 0102 governs a STANAG 4609 Edition 5 feed. The two rulings above are therefore the whole of the reconciliation; there is no third opinion to weigh.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.consistent_with_what_this_record_already: wrapper.the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical already reads 'Nothing. The wrapper states no field, no encoding, no layout and no requirement of its own.' This round asked a narrower question of the same five pages and got the same answer, which is a corroboration and not a new claim.
ruling_stanag_4609_edition_5.the_one_edition_disagreement_the_wrapper: Not about ST 0601 or ST 0102, and already recorded as ambiguity KLV 3: the wrapper is Edition 5 and MISP-2019.1's Appendix B reference [1] cites 'NATO STANAG 4609: NATO Digital Motion Imagery Standard, Edition 4, 19 Dec 2016' - the profile refers to the edition before the one that promulgates it. Re-read and confirmed verbatim this round.

outcome.why_the_stop_is_the_correct_outcome_and_: The round's first act was provenance and reconciliation precisely so that this could be decided before any tag was written down. It decided against proceeding on one document of two, on a rule this repository had already adopted, with the blocking condition documented and the reopen route named. A round that had transcribed 0601.19's tag table would have produced a table that looks authoritative, cites a real document, and is not the table the profile points at.

page_count_method.validated_before_it_was_trusted: Run against the seven documents whose page counts FORMAT_COVERAGE.md already records - eurocontrol-cat048-part4-edition-1-32.pdf 64, nato-aedp-4607-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 212, nato-aedp-4607-edition-a-v1.pdf 104, nato-stanag-4607-edition-4.pdf 6, nato-aedp-12-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 192, nato-aedp-12-edition-b-v2.pdf 150, nato-stanag-4676-edition-2.pdf 5 - and reproduced all seven exactly. The NATO documents keep their page objects inside compressed object streams and the EUROCONTROL one does not, so both paths are exercised by that check.
page_count_method.ruling: Ruled in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, 'The page count, ruled from what a reader does with the number'. A page count is one term of a pin's identity row and its job is to let someone holding a copy check they hold the same document - which they do by opening it and seeing how many pages it has. So the count is the number of pages the document HAS, which is the page tree; a raw-object scan counts FILE OBJECTS, a different quantity that coincides only when a file has no orphaned page objects and no incremental update.
page_count_method.what_this_record_used_to_say_and_why_it_: It used to read: 'Counted from each PDF's own page tree - occurrences of /Type /Page across raw objects and across every inflated object stream.' That sentence names the PAGE TREE and then defines a RAW-OBJECT SCAN, which are two different methods; it was self-contradictory from the day it was written and nothing noticed, because the two agree on any file with no orphaned page objects and no incremental update. CAT034 Phase 1 found the first file where they disagree and recorded the divergence; the harmonisation round ruled for the page tree and rewrote this field. THE COUNTS IN THIS RECORD DID NOT MOVE - both methods give them - so this is a correction to the description of how they were obtained and not to the values.
page_count_method.recomputed_under_the_ruling: Every document in this repository with a recorded page count was recomputed under both methods: 11 pins, 3 CAT034 lineage editions, 22 CAT048 lineage editions. No pin moved. Three CAT048 LINEAGE entries moved - editions 1.28 and 1.29 from 58 to 56, edition 1.30 from 59 to 57 - and cat048_pin.json records each as a correction with the ruling cited.
page_count_method.how_this_rounds_two_counts_were_produced: The ruled method, by a walker written for this round and validated before either number was trusted: run against the eight pins in this repository that are on disk and carry a recorded page count, it reproduced seven exactly - 31, 41, 64, 146, 5, 5 and 73. The eighth is the subject of the next field. Both new counts - ST 0601.19 at 226 and ST 0102.12 at 18 - are additionally method-INDEPENDENT: the retired raw-object scan returns the same numbers on both files, so neither rests on the ruling being right.
page_count_method.a_disagreement_found_outside_this_row_se: AND THE FIELD BELOW IS FALSE, at one document. recomputed_under_the_ruling says '11 pins ... No pin moved'. Validating this round's walker turned up a pin that does move: fixtures/cat062/spec/eurocontrol-asterix-cat062-p9-appendix-a-ed13.pdf is recorded as 25 pages and the ruled method gives 23. It is characterised, not guessed - the file holds 25 objects whose /Type is /Page, of which 23 are reachable from the catalog's /Pages tree; the two that are not, objects 1760 and 1782, each name a /Parent that IS reachable (1724 and 1727) whose /Kids array does not list them. That is exactly the orphaned-page-object case the ruling names, and 25 is the retired method's answer. The file's own top /Pages node states /Count 23. NOT CORRECTED HERE, deliberately: 25 is stated in cat062_pin.json and again in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's REF pin row, the two agree with each other, and moving a pin identity value for a format this round is not otherwise touching would be a re-measurement smuggled into a KLV commit. It is recorded at both sites that carry the false claim - here and in fft_pin.json - so that the claim and its known exception travel together, and the correction is a CAT062 decision.

A pin plus a hash plus a public retrieval route reproduces the artefact for any reader without this repository redistributing it, which is why EVERY adapter effort here pins rather than vendors. ambiguity_register.KLV 1: The promulgation lag. The wrapper's cover, Letter of Promulgation and reference are all dated 30 July 2020; the profile it promulgates carries November 2018 on its title page and in the footer of all 73 pages. Twenty months, unexplained in either document. Sharpened by the profile's own FORWARD versioning rule, which makes the '2019' in MISP-2019.1 an identifier rather than a date - so citing this content by year is ambiguous between 2018 printed, 2019 in the identifier and 2020 promulgated. Consequence adopted: every citation names the document by identifier and hash, never by date.
ambiguity_register.KLV 2: Every requirement ID inside MISP-2019.1 names an earlier profile version. 120 distinct requirement IDs occur and NONE is MISP-2019.1-nn. Distribution: MISP-2015.1 93, MISP-2018.1 17, MISP-2016.1 8, MISP-2018.3 4, MISP-2018.2 3, MISP-2017.1 3, MISP-2015.3 1. The prefix records the profile version that INTRODUCED the requirement, not the document carrying it, so MISP-2015.1-07 is a live requirement of MISP-2019.1. Consequence adopted: requirements are cited by their own ID with the pinned document named beside them, because an ID alone reads to a NATO reader as a citation of MISP-2015.1 - which STANAG 4609 Edition 4 promulgated and Edition 5 superseded.
ambiguity_register.KLV 3: The profile's reference to the STANAG is one edition behind and its Appendix C is one edition ahead. Appendix B ref [1] is 'NATO STANAG 4609: NATO Digital Motion Imagery Standard, Edition 4, 19 Dec 2016' and SS 1.1 sends the reader to [1] for NATO-specific requirements; Appendix C.1.2 discusses 'STANAG 4609 Edition 5 as represented in MISP-2019.1'. So within one document the STANAG is both Edition 4 and Edition 5, and the wrapper actually holding this profile is Edition 5, which supersedes Edition 4. A reader following SS 1.1's pointer lands on the superseded edition.
ambiguity_register.KLV 4: External context, and explicitly not an error: the NISP is a year behind the chain. NISP Volume 1, ADatP-34(L) / Version 12, 19 Jul 2019, 182 pages, lists NATO STANAG 4609 as 'Ed 4' against 'Standard - MISP-2015.1'. That NISP version predates STANAG 4609 Edition 5 by a year, so it is stale by chronology rather than by mistake - which means a programme taking the NISP as its authority would implement MISP-2015.1 and be conformant to a superseded STANAG. The copy read hashes to 12a3b2ab7075390b9edd53fb50538f5a7098c0d8f0a9a69c8af894acb40e1bac, 1440024 bytes, and is NOT in fixtures/klv/spec/ - so that hash stands on the reading that recorded it and is the one value here a later re-verification cannot check. Same treatment AEDP-12 Edition A (2014) gets in the NITS pin: history, never a basis.
ambiguity_register.KLV 5: The reference list versions most of its MISB documents and six not at all. A revision suffix is given for every document this row set relies on (0601.14, 0102.12, 0603.5, 0107.3, 0903.4, 0806.4, 1402.2, 1201.3, 1303.1, 1204.1, 0902.8) and none for ref [74] 'MISB ST 1607 Constructs to Amend/Segment KLV Metadata, 2016', ref [89] 'MISB ST 1101', ref [84] 'MISB RP 1302' or the three TRMs at refs [98], [99], [100]. ST 1607 is the one that bites: MISP-2017.1-95 is a 'shall' whose target names no revision.
ambiguity_register.KLV 6: Nothing in the profile requires a standalone metadata stream to carry an absolute time. The unconditional mandate MISP-2018.3-116 attaches to a Motion Imagery FRAME; the metadata mandate MISP-2018.1-97 is conditional on a timestamp being present; the prose in SS 2.1.5 introducing both is circular - 'it is also mandatory for Metadata packets which include a Metadata item for a timestamp based on Absolute Time'. The two unequivocal predecessors MISP-2015.1-03 and MISP-2015.1-04 are in Appendix A.2 as DEPRECATED. SS 5.5 then contemplates the case that falls through: 'There are situations where Metadata needs to be transmitted separately from the Motion Imagery.' Consequence: Event.observed_at for this format is not merely blocked on park 3, it may be absent from the source - which is gap 23.
ambiguity_register.KLV 7: The security mandate's paragraph and its requirement do not use the same term, and Appendix E defines both. SS 4.4.2.9 says 'It is mandatory that Motion Imagery Data be marked correctly and consistently with security classification' and 'The approved practices in this standard are mandatory for all Motion Imagery Data'; the requirement it introduces, MISP-2015.1-73, says 'Motion Imagery shall include Security Metadata'. Appendix E defines 'Motion Imagery Data' as 'Three components: Motion Imagery (see definition below), Metadata and/or Audio' and 'Motion Imagery' as a sequence of pictures. So the paragraph's scope includes a metadata stream and the requirement's scope is the imagery, which decides whether this adapter's input must be labelled at all.
ambiguity_register.KLV 8: The document classified as 'related' is the one that 'defines the required data items'. STANAG 4609 Ed 5 puts the Motion Imagery Handbook under OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS while its AGREEMENT clause names only MISP-2019.1, and MISP SS 1.3 calls the Handbook a companion 'providing definitions of terms used with more background and technical detail'. But SS 3.6.7 says of the same document that it 'defines the Structure of the Common Metadata System (CMS), describes how to organize the sensor/platform data into a hierarchy of KLV Packs and Local Sets that reduces the bandwidth needed to transmit the data, and defines the required data items'. A document that defines required data items is normative in fact. Park 10 records that whoever obtains it answers this first.
ambiguity_register.KLV 9: A pinned copy whose cover does not describe its contents, and the first ambiguity in this record found by a check nobody asked for. ST 0601.19's cover reads 'MISB ST 0601.19' and '02 March 2023'; its revision history table carries two rows dated AFTER that cover date - 05/10/2024, changing Figure 17's corner 4 tag values, and 06/11/2025, resolving 'item 42 ambiguity (i.e., MSL or HAE)' - and the file's /CreationDate is 2 July 2025. The document's own section 2 states the convention it is not following: a corrected document 'will have a single letter Minor Version appended to the Major Version number', as ST 0001.2 becomes ST 0001.2a, and the MISB 'will not update the referring document with the Minor Version number change'. So there exist at least three distinct documents all correctly cited as 'ST 0601.19', a citation by edition number cannot distinguish them, and the same section warns that 'when acquiring any MISB reference listed below from an NGA repository the latest version may be either a Major or Minor Version'. WHAT IT BOUNDS: it does not affect this round's ruling, which stops on .14-versus-.19 and would stop identically whichever .19 copy were held. What it bounds is the claim a pin makes - which is why this record's SHA-256 is the identity of a COPY and not of an edition, and this is the first document in this repository where those two come apart. ST 0102.12 was checked the same way and does not have the problem: one revision-history row, and it is the cover date.

That is materially weaker than the two blockers this repository already carries - GMTIF's Annex L, which reads '(TO BE PROVIDED)' in the promulgated text, and the NITS XSD, which the Custodian re-issues on its own revision axis and distributes through national representatives. parks.shared_exit_condition: For parks 1-7 and 9-12: obtain the EXACT version the delegation table pins (not 'the current one' - the profile pins a revision and a later revision is a different document); pin it in fixtures/klv/spec/ by SHA-256, byte count and page count with its title-page identity read; then write the row set that document supports.

the_one_that_is_not_a_download.reopen_condition: A PURCHASE DECISION, NOT A DOWNLOAD. SMPTE is a commercial standards body and ST 336 sits behind a paywall, which the profile concedes in its own register: 'Commercial references cited in this document are available from industry organizations.' The other eleven parks need somebody to spend an afternoon; this one needs somebody to spend money, and a table reporting both as 'obtain the document' would hide the only entry that has to go to a person with a budget.

what_this_phase_did_not_do: No adapter code, no codec, no fixtures, no golden files. Every mapping row in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md says `not yet`.
No mapping row was invented for any field whose layout lives in a document not held. That is the whole discipline of this phase and it is why the row set is short.

No gap was opened and no schema field proposed. Every absence is a DOCUMENT this repository does not hold rather than a CDM shortfall, and the two places where the CDM genuinely has nowhere to put something are already recorded as gap 18 and gap 23.

The premise that the MISP fixes the Precision Time Stamp's EPOCH was carried into this phase and is FALSE against the pinned copy: `epoch`, `1970`, `microsecond` and `leap` occur zero times in 73 pages, and the only timescale named is an example ('such as International Atomic Time (TAI)'). Recorded as a correction rather than quietly dropped.
